units.title: Remove registryManager direct import from calcDispatcher
units.description: calcDispatcher.ts line 9 imports registryManager directly — a layer violation. Route all registry access through engine calls instead. If calcDispatcher needs registry data, it should call an engine that wraps the registry, or use the service layer.

Registry access goes through engines or services

sessions.title: Direct File I/O Elimination + Misclassified Engine Cleanup
knowledge: 30 engines with readFileSync/readFile identified in audit
sessions.intent: Engines don't do their own file I/O. Data access goes through services or registries. Misclassified engines are reclassified. The hierarchy is clean end-to-end.

units.title: Classify 30 direct-I/O engines + identify misclassified engines
units.description: Read each of the 30 engines doing readFileSync/readFile. Classify each as: (A) should use existing registry, (B) should use existing service, (C) needs new service/registry, (D) legitimate I/O engine (FileStorageEngine, DiffEngine — their job IS file I/O). Also identify: (E) engines that are really data catalogs (SpindleProtectionEngine), (F) services with mixed concerns (CalculatorToolCribWorkspaceService). Category D engines are exempt from I/O cleanup.
units.four_loop: BUILD → SCRUTINIZE → GAP FILL → TIE UP
exit_criteria: 30 engines classified with rationale in a committed artifact
Category D exemptions justified with specific reasoning
Categories E and F identified with reclassification plan
Classification artifact committed to state/ or docs/

abort_criteria: Missing justification for any D/E/F classification
